benchmark_kind: single-host functional validation of the multi-page overflow path
protocol: MP-SPDZ Semi, three local parties, preprocessing included
scope_warning: Functional validation on one small synthetic fixture and one query, on a single host. It shows the overflow code path executes correctly; it is not a performance, MetaQA, WebQSP, WAN, or production result.
why_this_run_exists: Losslessness at high degree depends on overflow pages, and the earlier crossover and A/B fixtures both used pages_per_key=1, so the multi-page window read had never executed in MPC. That path contains the layout's most novel mechanism: a single demux serving a consecutive page window, where offset j reads the same pool shifted by j, with trailing dummy rows keeping shifted access in range and a secret page count masking pages past the end. Unit tests covered the layout builder, not the circuit.

layout.note: 3 edges per key into pages of 2 gives 2 pages with the second half full, so the run exercises offset 1 of the window, a page_count of 2 against other keys' 1, and the tail padding.

correctness.comparison: Exact JSON equality of all four reconstructed ranked rows against two independently implemented cleartext oracles.

what_this_does_not_show: Any performance claim; this fixture was sized for path coverage, not speed.
Any real-dataset, WAN, or multi-host result.
Any malicious-security property; MP-SPDZ Semi is passive-only.
